text:
alex: quick question — hit an ambiguous match in staging. three routes in the routing table and i want opinions on precedence (host wildcards, path captures, header overrides).

alex: routes (simplified):
```
- route A:
  host: "*.company.internal"
  path: /api/v1/users/(.*)
  service: users-v2

- route B:
  host: "api.company.internal"
  path: /api/(?<svc>v1)/users
  service: users-v1

- route C (header anchor):
  host: "*.company.internal"
  path: /api/.*
  header_anchor: { name: "x-service", value: "users-v1" }
  service: users-v1
```

alex: request: host=api.company.internal, path=/api/v1/users/123, header x-service=users-v1
Which route should win? currently staging picked route C (header) and routed to users-v1 even though route B has an exact host. feels odd.

maria: i repro'd. our matcher treats header anchors as exact and scored them before host specificity. that's probably why.

kevin: IMO we need a deterministic scoring matrix. naive priority list leads to surprises. proposal: weight host specificity > path specificity > header anchors, but allow an exact header "service binding" to beat a wildcard host.

natalie: console UX request: when a tie or surprising winner happens, show a "match_score" trace with breakdown. e.g. host segments=+16, path segments=+8, header anchor=+4, capture penalty=-1. simple visible numbers will remove magic.

sven: captures should reduce specificity. e.g. any regex capture in path or host -> apply -1 per capture token. otherwise people will prefer complex regexes to win.

alex: short RFC draft i'm leaning to: \n- compute score components: host_exactness (segments*8), path_specificity (segments*4), header_anchor (exact match +6, anchor presence +3), captures penalty (-2 per capture), explicit service name tie-breaker (+1).
- final tie-break: prefer route with explicit service (not alias). then stable sort by creation ts.

kevin: +1 to deterministic numeric approach. suggest header_anchor exact match = +6 though, so it only beats wildcard host when appropriate.

deploy-bot: test run: 1726504332 - request abc123 -> matched route B (users-v1) (reason: host_exact=+16, path_exact=+8, header_anchor_exact=+6, capture_penalty=-2 => total=28)
(note: earlier staging used different weights which favored header-only route)

maria: :thumbsup: good. also let's add fallback semantics: if header claims a service that has no backing cluster, we should continue evaluating other matches rather than immediately 404.

natalie: console should show losing candidates with their score lines and which component beat them. small UX: a popover "why matched" next to route in trace.

alex: i'll put up a PR with the scoring table + tests and a small console patch to show scoring. assigning to @kevin for matcher impl review.

kevin: i'll review tomorrow. one more nit: document how this interacts with pinned rollout policies (can an explicit rollout tag override match?). we should consider that but keep scoring separate from rollout rules.

sven: logging: add a short-match-reason header in responses for internal clients (x-redwood-match: users-v1;reason=host+16,path+8,header+6) to speed debugging.

alex: great. thanks everyone — will open RFC/PRs.
